pages.title: High agreeableness: supporting cooperation without erasing your boundaries
pages.summary: A high agreeableness result suggests frequent compassion, respectful restraint, or willingness to trust and cooperate; it does not measure kindness, morality, weakness, or relationship success.
pages.meaning: This range points to a relatively strong tendency to consider other people's needs, preserve respectful interaction, and begin with cooperative assumptions. Compassion, respectfulness, and trust can differ, so a broad result does not require agreeing with everyone, avoiding conflict, or trusting without evidence.
pages.possible_patterns: You may notice the human cost of a decision, soften a disagreement enough to keep dialogue open, share credit, or help before being asked. Costs can appear when requests become obligations by default, your dissent arrives too late, or preserving harmony hides unequal effort and unclear consent.
pages.counterexample: Someone in this range can refuse a request, question a person's motives, negotiate firmly, report harmful conduct, or end an unfair relationship. High agreeableness describes recurring cooperative and considerate tendencies, not compliance, gullibility, or the absence of anger.
pages.context_variation: Cooperation may be more visible when relationships feel reciprocal, roles are clear, and disagreement is safe. Exploitation, repeated broken promises, time pressure, power imbalance, or responsibility for protecting others can produce sharper boundaries without invalidating the underlying result.
pages.combination_effects: With higher conscientiousness, care may become reliable follow-through and stewardship; with lower conscientiousness, good intentions may exceed delivered help. Higher extraversion can make warmth and mediation more visible, while lower extraversion may express consideration through listening, preparation, and private support.
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: Potential strengths include building trust, reducing unnecessary friction, and representing needs that are easy to overlook. Tradeoffs can include overaccommodation, indirect dissent, untested trust, resentment after silent giving, or difficulty making decisions that impose unavoidable costs. Context determines the useful balance.
pages.communication_action: For the next request, answer with one of three explicit responses: yes, no, or yes under stated conditions. Name your own constraint before offering help, check who owns the outcome, and schedule a point to revisit the agreement rather than relying on unspoken goodwill.
pages.not_meaning: This result does not mean morally better, always kind, conflict-free, naive, weak, self-sacrificing, easy to manage, or guaranteed to have healthy relationships. It is not a diagnosis, hiring rule, safety clearance, or proof that another person deserves trust.
pages.method_boundary: A range label compresses a continuous self-report result and can hide facet differences, cultural politeness rules, power, safety, and current relationship history. Interpret repeated choices and meaningful exceptions; group research cannot certify one person's motives or turn cooperation into a fixed duty.

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto & John (2017), BFI-2 domains and facets
visible_sources.limitation: Supports a named hierarchical trait model, not the accuracy or morality of an individual FermatMind range result.

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts, Walton, & Viechtbauer (2006), personality trait change
visible_sources.limitation: Reports group-level patterns across studies; it does not predict how or whether one person's result will change.

pages.title: 宜人性较高：支持合作，也保留清楚的个人边界
pages.summary: 宜人性较高表示你较常表现出同情、尊重克制，或愿意从信任与合作开始，但不代表善良等级、软弱、顺从或关系一定成功。
pages.meaning: 这个区间提示你较常考虑他人需要、维护尊重互动，并用合作假设开始关系。同情、尊重与信任三个侧面可能并不整齐，所以总分较高不要求你同意所有人、回避冲突或在没有证据时继续相信。
pages.possible_patterns: 你可能较早看见决策对人的代价、让分歧保持可对话、主动分享功劳，或在对方开口前提供帮助。代价可能出现在请求默认变成义务、异议太晚才出现，或为了和谐掩盖投入不均与同意不清。
pages.counterexample: 宜人性较高的人仍可拒绝请求、质疑动机、坚定谈判、报告伤害行为，或离开不公平关系。这个结果描述重复出现的合作与体谅倾向，不是顺从、轻信或永远不会愤怒。
pages.context_variation: 当关系互惠、角色清楚且分歧安全时，合作通常更明显；被利用、承诺反复落空、时间压力、权力不对等，或需要保护他人时，同一个人也会建立更锋利的边界。
pages.combination_effects: 与较高尽责性组合时，关心更可能变成稳定跟进与照料；与较低尽责性组合时，帮助意愿可能超过实际交付。较高外向性会让温暖与调解更可见，较低外向性则可能通过倾听、准备和私下支持表达体谅。
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: 潜在优势是建立信任、减少无谓摩擦，并代表容易被忽略的需要；潜在代价是过度迁就、间接表达异议、未经检验地信任、长期付出后积累怨气，或难以执行必然让部分人承担成本的决定。
pages.communication_action: 面对下一项请求，只用三个明确答案之一回应：同意、拒绝，或满足条件时同意。先说出自己的限制，再确认结果由谁负责，并约定复查协议的时间，不要只依赖没有说出口的善意。
pages.not_meaning: 它不代表品德更高、永远善良、没有冲突、天真、软弱、自我牺牲、容易管理或必然拥有健康关系。它不是医疗诊断、招聘规则、安全许可，也不能证明某个人值得信任。
pages.method_boundary: 区间标签压缩了连续自评结果，也可能遮住侧面差异、文化礼貌规则、权力、安全感与关系历史。解释时要同时寻找重复选择和重要反例，不能用群体研究证明个人动机或把合作固定成义务。

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto 与 John（2017）：BFI-2 维度与侧面
visible_sources.limitation: 支持明确命名的层级特质模型，不证明个人费马测试区间结果准确或品德高低。

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts、Walton 与 Viechtbauer（2006）：人格特质变化
visible_sources.limitation: 报告跨研究的群体变化模式，不能预测某个个人是否或如何变化。

pages.title: Middle agreeableness: adjusting cooperation to evidence and relationship
pages.summary: A middle agreeableness result is a selective cooperation pattern, not an absence of character: trust, accommodation, and directness may shift with evidence, stakes, reciprocity, and role.
pages.meaning: This range suggests that accommodation and challenge are both available strategies. The threshold can change with relationship history, consequence, evidence of good faith, responsibility, and whether the task needs cohesion or scrutiny. It may also reflect mixed facets rather than uniformly middle scores.
pages.possible_patterns: You may cooperate quickly with a proven partner, ask harder questions in a new arrangement, compromise on preferences but not principles, or trust someone in one domain while verifying them in another. Others may see warmth in one setting and skepticism in another because the decision rule changed.
pages.counterexample: One generous act does not establish a high range, and one blunt disagreement does not establish a low range. Someone here can defend another person's needs strongly or make a competitive choice when roles, evidence, and consequences justify it.
pages.context_variation: Reciprocity, shared goals, clear accountability, and repair after mistakes may lower the threshold for trust. Ambiguous ownership, repeated boundary crossing, scarce resources, or incentives to misrepresent can raise it. The useful observation is what changes the cooperation rule.
pages.combination_effects: Higher neuroticism may increase caution after ambiguous social signals, while lower neuroticism may make repair easier to attempt. Higher openness can support perspective-taking across unfamiliar values; lower openness may make cooperation stronger inside established norms and relationships.
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: Potential strengths include matching trust to evidence, translating between harmony and challenge, and resisting both automatic suspicion and automatic compliance. Tradeoffs can include appearing inconsistent, leaving expectations implicit, or deciding case by case without a principle others can understand.
pages.communication_action: For one live collaboration, write the evidence that would increase trust, the boundary that would reduce it, and the repair required after a breach. Share at least one of those conditions before conflict appears, then review whether your response matched the stated rule.
pages.not_meaning: Middle does not mean morally average, indecisive, emotionally neutral, perfectly fair, equally trusting everywhere, or without a recognizable relationship pattern. It does not guarantee balance and must not become a diagnosis, hiring judgment, or compatibility forecast.
pages.method_boundary: A cut label cannot show the exact score, uncertainty, facet profile, power conditions, or relationship evidence behind a response. Use it to investigate cooperation thresholds across comparable situations, not to claim a universal midpoint or judge one decision by trait alone.

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto & John (2017), BFI-2 domains and facets
visible_sources.limitation: Supports hierarchical trait measurement, not a universal meaning for every middle-range score.

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts, Walton, & Viechtbauer (2006), personality trait change
visible_sources.limitation: Group-level change evidence does not establish individual score movement or explain one context shift.

pages.title: 宜人性中间区间：让合作程度跟随证据与关系变化
pages.summary: 中间区间具有明确的选择性合作模式：信任、迁就和直接表达会随证据、后果、互惠与角色变化，而不是没有稳定特点。
pages.meaning: 这个区间说明迁就与挑战都可能成为你的可用策略，选择哪一个会受关系历史、后果、善意证据、责任和任务更需要凝聚还是审查影响。它也可能来自三个侧面强弱不同，而不是每项都正好居中。
pages.possible_patterns: 你可能与经验证的伙伴快速合作，在新安排中提出更难的问题；也可能在偏好上让步、在原则上坚持，或在一个领域信任某人、在另一个领域继续核验。不同场景因此会留下不同印象。
pages.counterexample: 一次慷慨行为不能证明宜人性很高，一次直白分歧也不能证明宜人性很低。中间区间的人可以坚定保护他人需要，也可以在角色、证据和后果要求时做竞争性选择。
pages.context_variation: 互惠、共同目标、清楚问责和错误后的修复会降低信任门槛；责任含糊、边界反复被越过、资源稀缺或存在误导激励时，门槛会上升。需要观察的是哪项条件改变了合作规则。
pages.combination_effects: 较高神经质可能在含糊社交信号后增加谨慎，较低神经质则可能更容易尝试修复。较高开放性支持理解陌生价值，较低开放性则可能让合作在既有规范和熟悉关系中更稳定。
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: 潜在优势是让信任匹配证据、在和谐与挑战之间翻译，并避免自动怀疑或自动顺从；潜在代价是看起来前后不一、没有说明期待，或总是个案判断却不给别人可理解的原则。
pages.communication_action: 面对一次正在进行的合作，写下什么证据会增加信任、什么边界会降低信任，以及违约后需要什么修复。冲突出现前至少公开一个条件，之后复盘自己的回应是否符合原先规则。
pages.not_meaning: 中间区间不代表品德普通、优柔寡断、情感中性、绝对公平、处处同样信任或没有关系模式。它不自动保证平衡，也不能被换算成医疗诊断、招聘判断或关系匹配预测。
pages.method_boundary: 区间切分无法显示精确分数、不确定性、侧面组合、权力条件和关系证据。它适合帮助你调查可比较场景中的合作门槛，不适合宣称所有关系都稳定居中，也不能单靠特质评价一次决定。

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto 与 John（2017）：BFI-2 维度与侧面
visible_sources.limitation: 支持层级特质测量，不代表所有中间区间分数都有同一种含义。

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts、Walton 与 Viechtbauer（2006）：人格特质变化
visible_sources.limitation: 群体变化证据不能证明个人分数移动，也不能解释一次情境差异。

pages.title: Low agreeableness: using skepticism and directness without contempt
pages.summary: A low agreeableness result suggests less frequent accommodation, trusting assumptions, or compassionate restraint; it does not mean cruel, dishonest, unsafe, selfish, or incapable of care.
pages.meaning: This range points to a relatively stronger preference for questioning claims, protecting self-interest, competing openly, or stating disagreement without extensive softening. Facets can diverge: someone may distrust motives yet follow respectful rules, or speak bluntly while showing practical compassion in high-need situations.
pages.possible_patterns: You may identify weak assumptions, negotiate firmly, resist pressure to agree, or prioritize the decision over emotional smoothness. Risks can appear when accuracy is used to dismiss impact, skepticism becomes a default verdict, respect is treated as inefficiency, or others cannot distinguish challenge from hostility.
pages.counterexample: A person in this range can be loyal, generous, ethical, protective, and deeply caring toward chosen people or causes. Lower agreeableness is not proof of cruelty, manipulation, lack of empathy, antisocial behavior, or inability to cooperate under clear terms.
pages.context_variation: Directness may rise in competitive, high-accountability, low-trust, or technically exact settings. It may soften with vulnerable people, demonstrated reciprocity, shared identity, or consequences that require repair. A harsher environment can also reward defensive skepticism that does not appear elsewhere.
pages.combination_effects: With higher conscientiousness, skepticism may become documented review and consistent standards; with lower conscientiousness, challenge may occur without follow-through. Higher extraversion can make disagreement public and rapid, while lower extraversion may express it through selective refusals, written critique, or withdrawal.
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: Potential strengths include resisting group pressure, exposing weak reasoning, protecting boundaries, and making tradeoffs explicit. Tradeoffs can include trust erosion, avoidable conflict, reduced information sharing, or overlooking emotional and relational evidence that affects execution. Directness still needs design.
pages.communication_action: In the next disagreement, separate the claim, evidence, impact, and relationship. State the disputed claim without labeling the person, ask what evidence would change either view, and name one repair step if your delivery caused unnecessary harm even when the substantive point remains.
pages.not_meaning: This result does not mean cruel, immoral, dishonest, dangerous, selfish, incapable of empathy, unable to collaborate, or suited to adversarial work. It is not a diagnosis, risk assessment, hiring exclusion, excuse for harm, or prediction of relationship failure.
pages.method_boundary: Self-report ranges can reflect norms, incentives, trust history, power, and conflict exposure as well as recurring tendencies. Compare similar situations and seek behavioral feedback; do not infer intent, safety, or a clinical condition from a group-level trait label.

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto & John (2017), BFI-2 domains and facets
visible_sources.limitation: Supports a named domain-and-facet structure, not a moral, safety, or clinical judgment about one individual.

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts, Walton, & Viechtbauer (2006), personality trait change
visible_sources.limitation: Aggregated change estimates do not prescribe an intervention or guarantee individual change.

pages.title: 宜人性较低：使用怀疑与直接表达，但不滑向轻蔑
pages.summary: 宜人性较低表示你较少迁就、预设信任或用同情克制表达，但不代表残忍、不诚实、不安全、自私或没有关心他人的能力。
pages.meaning: 这个区间提示你可能更偏好质疑说法、保护自身利益、公开竞争，或不经大量软化就表达分歧。三个侧面仍可能分开：有人不轻信动机却严格遵守尊重规则，也有人说话直接，却在高需要场景给予实际帮助。
pages.possible_patterns: 你可能迅速指出薄弱假设、坚定谈判、抵抗同意压力，或把决策置于情绪平顺之前。风险可能出现在用准确性否定影响、把怀疑变成默认判决、把尊重当成低效，或让别人无法区分挑战与敌意。
pages.counterexample: 宜人性较低的人仍可忠诚、慷慨、守伦理、保护他人，并深切关心自己选择的人与事业。较低结果不能证明残忍、操控、缺少同理、反社会行为或无法在清楚条件下合作。
pages.context_variation: 竞争、高问责、低信任或技术精确场景会提高直接程度；面对脆弱群体、已证明的互惠、共同身份或需要修复的后果时，表达可能软化。严苛环境也会奖励在其他地方不常出现的防御性怀疑。
pages.combination_effects: 与较高尽责性组合时，怀疑可能变成记录充分的审查与一致标准；与较低尽责性组合时，挑战可能缺少后续。较高外向性会让分歧公开而迅速，较低外向性则可能通过选择性拒绝、书面批评或退出表达。
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: 潜在优势是抵抗群体压力、暴露薄弱推理、保护边界并公开真实取舍；潜在代价是侵蚀信任、制造可避免冲突、减少信息分享，或忽略会影响执行的情感与关系证据。直接表达仍需要设计。
pages.communication_action: 下一次分歧把主张、证据、影响和关系分开；在不贴人标签的情况下陈述争议，询问什么证据会改变双方看法，并在表达造成不必要伤害时提出一项修复，即使实质观点不变。
pages.not_meaning: 它不代表残忍、没有道德、不诚实、危险、自私、无法同理、不能协作或适合所有对抗性工作。它不是医疗诊断、风险评估、招聘排除、伤害借口或关系失败预测。
pages.method_boundary: 自评区间会同时受到规范、激励、信任历史、权力和冲突经历影响。要比较相似情境并寻求行为反馈，不能用群体特质标签推断个人意图、安全性或临床状况。

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto 与 John（2017）：BFI-2 维度与侧面
visible_sources.limitation: 支持明确命名的维度与侧面结构，不支持对个人做品德、安全或临床判断。

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts、Walton 与 Viechtbauer（2006）：人格特质变化
visible_sources.limitation: 汇总变化估计不能规定个人干预，也不能保证某个人发生改变。

pages.title: High agreeableness helping audit: protect reciprocity, consent, and capacity
pages.summary: This legacy page is a helping-boundary protocol for people whose cooperation has become hard to evaluate: map consent, ownership, reciprocity, capacity, and a clear stopping point.
pages.meaning: Use this page when helping is frequent but it is unclear whether the support is requested, reciprocal, sustainable, or replacing another person's responsibility. The task is not to become less caring; it is to make generosity observable and revisable rather than silently compulsory.
pages.possible_patterns: You may accept work before checking capacity, solve a problem the owner needed to learn from, avoid naming resentment, or keep an agreement alive after reciprocity disappeared. Others can then depend on support whose limits were never stated, making both trust and delivery fragile.
pages.counterexample: Unequal help is not automatically unhealthy during illness, crisis, caregiving, or an explicit gift. The audit should preserve chosen generosity while questioning assistance driven by fear of disappointment, unclear ownership, assumed consent, or a promise no one actually made.
pages.context_variation: Boundary strain rises in vague roles, unequal power, repeated emergencies, and cultures where refusal carries social cost. It may fall when requests are explicit, recipients retain agency, responsibilities have owners, and no is treated as information rather than rejection.
pages.combination_effects: Higher conscientiousness can make help dependable but also convert every request into a tracked obligation; lower conscientiousness may produce warm offers that exceed follow-through. Higher neuroticism can make possible disappointment feel urgent, increasing the value of a pause before answering.
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: A helping audit can preserve compassion, cooperation, and relationship trust while reducing hidden obligation. The tradeoff is tolerating another person's frustration, allowing them to solve some problems differently, and accepting that a boundary can be caring even when it is not immediately pleasing.
pages.communication_action: List current help commitments with requester, owner, consent, capacity cost, reciprocity expectation, and end condition. Renegotiate one item whose owner or endpoint is unclear, then use a pause phrase before new requests so that agreement follows a real capacity check.
pages.not_meaning: This audit does not label generosity as weakness, require equal exchange in every relationship, excuse abandonment, or prove codependence. The range is not a diagnosis, moral credential, consent substitute, or guarantee that helping is experienced as helpful.
pages.method_boundary: The protocol is an editorial reflection tool, not a validated treatment or individualized relationship assessment. Care obligations, disability, culture, resources, and power can dominate behavior; use explicit agreements and feedback rather than assigning cause to personality alone.

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto & John (2017), BFI-2 domains and facets
visible_sources.limitation: Provides domain-and-facet terminology, not validation of this helping-boundary protocol.

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts, Walton, & Viechtbauer (2006), personality trait change
visible_sources.limitation: Group-level change research does not show that this audit will change an individual's trait or relationship.

pages.title: Low agreeableness disagreement protocol: keep challenge direct and repairable
pages.summary: This legacy page is a direct-disagreement protocol: isolate the claim, test evidence, state impact, preserve respect, decide the issue, and repair avoidable relational damage.
pages.meaning: Use this page when skepticism or direct challenge serves the decision but the exchange risks becoming personal, contemptuous, or impossible to repair. The objective is not softer agreement. It is to keep disagreement specific enough that evidence can change the decision and people can continue working afterward.
pages.possible_patterns: A weak proposal may trigger a verdict about the proposer, speed may replace a shared definition of the dispute, or emotional impact may be dismissed as irrelevant. The substantive issue then becomes harder to resolve because participants must defend identity, status, or safety at the same time.
pages.counterexample: Firm refusal, whistleblowing, urgent correction, and naming harm may require uncomfortable language. Repair does not mean withdrawing a true claim or restoring every relationship; it means removing avoidable distortion and owning delivery choices that were not necessary to the point.
pages.context_variation: The protocol matters most under time pressure, status conflict, repeated error, public scrutiny, or low trust. In unsafe or abusive conditions, direct engagement may not be appropriate; documentation, escalation, distance, or external support can be the safer form of action.
pages.combination_effects: Higher conscientiousness can support evidence and follow-through but may make standards feel nonnegotiable; lower conscientiousness can leave criticism without a repair plan. Higher extraversion may accelerate live conflict, while lower extraversion may benefit from written claims and a scheduled response.
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: A repairable disagreement can preserve scrutiny, boundary clarity, and honest tradeoffs while reducing unnecessary trust loss. Its tradeoff is spending time on shared definitions and impact, accepting that being substantively right does not make every delivery effective, and tolerating unresolved difference.
pages.communication_action: Write the disputed claim in one sentence, list the evidence and decision consequence, then remove labels about the person's character. During the exchange, ask for the strongest contrary evidence; afterward, state any delivery harm you own and what will change next time.
pages.not_meaning: This protocol does not require appeasement, promise reconciliation, excuse aggression, or imply that all viewpoints deserve equal weight. A lower range is not a diagnosis, danger score, moral failure, hiring exclusion, or permission to disregard consent and dignity.
pages.method_boundary: This sequence is a practical editorial tool, not a clinically validated intervention or evidence that one trait caused the conflict. Power, discrimination, incentives, safety, skills, and organizational rules may be decisive; keep the range as one hypothesis among several.

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto & John (2017), BFI-2 domains and facets
visible_sources.limitation: Provides trait terminology, not proof that a score caused conflict or that this protocol is effective.

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts, Walton, & Viechtbauer (2006), personality trait change
visible_sources.limitation: Aggregated personality change findings do not validate this disagreement sequence for an individual.
